summary: Independently re-verified the software-engineer's SEC-4 close-out (extending server-resolved paid-feature region gating from /duel and /duel/chips to /tournaments). All claims in the prior handoff hold up under independent re-derivation, not just re-reading: (1) rendering-mode flip confirmed myself via a fresh detached worktree build at HEAD (412f6f3, unmodified) vs the working tree (with the three uncommitted changes) — baseline route table shows `o /tournaments`, modified shows `f /tournaments`, prerender-manifest.json diff shows exactly `removed: ['/tournaments']` / `added: []`, and a full 125-line route-table diff between both builds shows exactly one line changed. (2) TournamentList.tsx's render is a single top-level ternary `!user ? SignInGate : !geoAllowed ? region-block : tier-picker+queue-UI` with no other branch, early return, or second render path — the tier-picker/queue UI is only reachable when both user and geoAllowed are truthy, matching the property already verified for ChipDuelLobby last cycle. Confirmed via read, not inference. (3) The new queue-route guard (assertPaidDuelAllowed + 403 GEO_BLOCKED envelope) is structurally byte-identical in call, position (after requireAuth, before checkRateLimit), and JSON envelope shape to both app/app/api/tournaments/[id]/checkout/route.ts and .../register/route.ts, confirmed by direct side-by-side read of all three files. Import depth (4 levels vs siblings' 5) is correct because queue/route.ts is not nested under [id]/. Confirmed the guard is genuinely unreachable today (comingSoon() 503 early-return still precedes it, file still @ts-nocheck) and did not write or expect a runtime 403 test against it, per the software-engineer's caveat. (4) Grepped all of app/ for TournamentList usage: the only caller is app/app/tournaments/page.tsx, which supplies the required initialGeoAllowed prop — no other call site was missed. (5) No new unit tests were added. Reasoning: the page's only new logic is a call to the already-fully-tested resolveRankedEligibility (covered by app/src/__tests__/rankedEligibility.test.ts, kill-switch + all geo branches, unchanged by this diff — /tournaments is just a new caller of existing, tested logic, same as /duel was). The queue-route guard is unreachable dead code by the software-engineer's own correct design constraint (enabling it is a separate product decision); a test asserting 403 there would be meaningless (the live behavior is 503) and a test asserting 503-still-happens would not exercise the new lines at all. TournamentList.tsx and ChipDuelLobby.tsx both have zero pre-existing render tests — this is the same gap the prior cycle's verifier/reviewer/qa-acceptance already agreed was a pre-existing, non-blocking gap for ChipDuelLobby/DuelHome, not something this diff introduced or is obligated to backfill. Recording this explicitly as a gap rather than forcing a low-value test. (6) Ran all six gates fresh myself: app-lint, app-typecheck, app-test (80 files/745 tests), orchestrator-typecheck, orchestrator-test (15 suites/58 tests), pack-hygiene — all green. Per testing.md's 'a gate is not a gate until proven to fail' rule: temporarily deleted the initialGeoAllowed prop from the TournamentsPage render call and re-ran pnpm typecheck — it failed with TS2741 'Property initialGeoAllowed is missing... but required in type TournamentListProps', proving app-typecheck genuinely catches a caller that fails to wire the server-derived prop (the exact defect class this whole change exists to prevent). Reverted the probe immediately; diff confirmed identical to the pre-probe state (17 insertions/2 deletions in page.tsx, matching software-engineer's original diff) and typecheck re-confirmed clean. I did not find a way to make a gate red for the queue-route guard specifically, because it is dead code by design (no test can invoke it meaningfully) — being honest about that rather than fabricating a check. (7) Reverted app/next-env.d.ts churn caused by my own two pnpm build runs (confirmed dirty via git status, reverted with git checkout --, re-ran pnpm typecheck clean afterward) and removed the scratch git worktree. Final git status shows only the four originally-intended file changes plus the untracked software-engineer handoff file — no residue from my verification work.

testGaps.gap: TournamentList.tsx and ChipDuelLobby.tsx have zero pre-existing render/component tests (no React Testing Library harness exercises either component's ternary branches directly).
testGaps.whyNotAdded: This is a pre-existing gap in the codebase, not something this diff introduced — it predates this change and predates the /duel geo-gating change last cycle, where the prior verifier/reviewer/qa-acceptance already agreed it was non-blocking for the structurally-identical ChipDuelLobby. The structural soundness of the new ternary is fully verifiable by direct reading (single ternary, no alternate path), which is why this verifier confirmed it that way rather than fabricating a shallow render test with no prior harness to build on.
testGaps.recommendation: If a component-test harness is introduced for this component family in a future cycle, add render tests for TournamentList, ChipDuelLobby, and DuelHome together, asserting: signed-out shows SignInGate, signed-in+blocked shows region-restricted block, signed-in+allowed shows the paid UI. Out of scope for this change.

testGaps.gap: The new queue-route guard in app/app/api/tournaments/queue/route.ts has no automated test.
testGaps.whyNotAdded: The guard is unreachable dead code today (comingSoon() 503 precedes it in both GET and POST, file is @ts-nocheck). A test invoking the handler observes 503 regardless of the new guard's presence or correctness, so it would prove nothing about the guard. A test that removes the comingSoon() return to make the guard reachable would be testing code that isn't shipped this way, and per the software-engineer's explicit, correct instruction, removing that early return is a separate product decision out of scope here.
testGaps.recommendation: When a future change removes the comingSoon() early return to actually enable tournaments, that PR must add a runtime test asserting 403 GEO_BLOCKED for a blocked region on POST /api/tournaments/queue, mirroring whatever tests exist (or should exist) for the checkout/register siblings at that time.

learnings.insight: Re-deriving the rendering-mode claim independently (fresh worktree + fresh build) rather than trusting the prior handoff's numbers caught nothing wrong this cycle, but it did surface a minor discrepancy worth noting: my route-table line count was 125, not the 136 the software-engineer reported. Both counts are consistent (different capture regex/grep boundaries around wrapped lines and the Proxy/Middleware footer) and both independently show exactly ONE line changed, so the underlying claim holds — but a raw line-count in a handoff should not be treated as a checksum across differently-shaped capture scripts.
learnings.action: When comparing route-table line counts across two different agents' capture scripts, compare which single route changed (the load-bearing fact), not the raw total line count, since capture regex differences (footer lines, wrapped continuation lines) shift totals without indicating a real discrepancy.

learnings.insight: For a change whose only new logic is 'call an already-fully-tested pure function from a new call site' (resolveRankedEligibility from /tournaments, same as it's already called from /duel), the correct verification is confirming the call site is wired correctly (types + structural read + build-mode proof), not writing a duplicate unit test of the already-tested function. Forcing a new test here would just re-test rankedEligibility.test.ts's existing coverage under a different file name.
learnings.action: Before asking for 'a new test' on a change, check whether the diff introduces new logic or is purely a new caller of existing, tested logic. New callers of tested pure functions need caller-correctness verification (types, structural read, build-mode proof for rendering claims), not parallel unit tests.

learnings.insight: Second consecutive cycle where a security-reviewer-filed, non-blocking ledger open-question was closed cleanly on the first software-engineer attempt with all gates green and no verifier findings requiring loop-back. The 'file as ledger entry, don't block' pattern for same-defect-class findings on out-of-scope/unreachable code continues to work.
learnings.action: No action needed; continue trusting this deferral pattern when the finding records the exact reachability condition, as SEC-4 did.
